title: Grades 3–5 Practice Test — Form B
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: Four-domain classroom practice in listening, reading, speaking, and writing. Work at your own pace. Item difficulty, scoring, timing, and routing are not equivalent to ACCESS.

sections.title: Listening: Career Day
sections.directions: You will hear a teacher or a visitor talk. Press play to listen. You can listen again if you need to. Then answer each question. Choose the best answer.

items.title: Where the Firefighter Works
script: Hello, everyone! I am Captain Diallo, and I am a firefighter. My job is to keep people safe from fires. I work at the fire station on Park Street.
At the station, we check our trucks and hoses every morning. We also practice climbing ladders. When the alarm rings, we put on our gear in less than two minutes.
Here is an important safety rule. If you hear a smoke alarm at home, get out fast and stay out. Never go back inside for toys. Meet your family at a safe spot outside, like a big tree or a mailbox.
items.correct: Correct. Captain Diallo works at the fire station on Park Street.
items.hint: Listen to the beginning, when he says "I work at…"

items.title: Story Time
items.prompt: When is Story Time at the library?
script: Good morning! I am Ms. Kim, and I am a librarian at the Riverside Library. A librarian helps people find books and information.
Every Saturday at ten o'clock, we have Story Time for children. On Wednesdays after school, we have a homework club where students can get help with math and reading.
Did you know that a library card is free? To get one, bring a grown-up and a letter with your address. With your card, you can borrow up to five books for three weeks.
items.correct: Correct. Story Time is every Saturday at ten o'clock.
items.hint: Listen for a day of the week and a time.
items.support: Two different events are named. Match Story Time with its day.

sections.title: Reading: Weather Through the Seasons
sections.directions: Read the passage. Then answer the questions. You can look back at the passage, the picture, and the chart as many times as you want.

items.title: The Tree in Fall
items.prompt: Look at the pictures of the maple tree. What does the tree look like in fall?

options.text: It has orange and red leaves.

picture.alt: The same maple tree in four seasons, from left to right. In spring, it has light green leaves and pink flowers. In summer, it is full of dark green leaves under a hot sun. In fall, its leaves are orange and red and falling to the ground. In winter, its branches are bare and snow covers the ground.

passage: In many places, the weather changes during the year. These changes make four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter. One maple tree can show us how each season is different.
In spring, the air gets warmer and it rains often. The maple tree grows small, light green leaves and pink flowers. Rain and sunshine help plants grow quickly.
Summer is the hottest season. The days are long, and the sun shines for many hours. The maple tree is full of big, dark green leaves. People like to rest in its cool shade.
In fall, the days get shorter and the air gets cooler. The maple leaves turn orange and red. Then they drop to the ground.
Winter is the coldest season. The maple tree has no leaves, and its branches are bare. Sometimes snow falls and covers the ground. The tree rests until spring comes again.
items.correct: Correct. In fall, the maple leaves turn orange and red.
items.hint: Read paragraph 4, then find the matching picture.
items.support: The pictures go in order: spring, summer, fall, winter.

sections.title: Speaking: Helpers in Our Community
sections.directions: Look at each picture. Read how the model student started. Plan your ideas, then say your answer out loud in full sentences. Use the word bank to help you.

items.title: Community Helpers on the Street
passage: A model student, Amina, started like this: "I see a crossing guard. She is holding a stop sign."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the picture of the street. Who are the community helpers? What is each helper doing? Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the picture of the street. Who are the community helpers? What is each helper doing?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
sayFor: tell what each helper is doing
tell how a helper helps people

models.B: I see a crossing guard with a stop sign. A mail carrier puts a letter in the mailbox. A baker has bread. A bus driver drives a bus.
models.C: This picture shows a busy street with many community helpers. The crossing guard is holding up a stop sign so two children can cross the street safely. Next to her, a mail carrier is putting a letter in a blue mailbox, and a baker is standing in front of the bakery with a loaf of bread. A bus driver is driving people around town.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): This picture shows a busy street with many community helpers. The crossing guard is holding up a stop sign so two children can cross the street safely. Next to her, a mail carrier is putting a letter in a blue mailbox, and a baker is standing in front of the bakery with a loaf of bread. A bus driver is driving people around town.
items.hint: Point to each helper. Say what the helper is doing.

items.title: The Lost Puppy
passage: A model student, Kofi, started like this: "First, the boy's puppy was missing."
Now it is your turn. Plan your ideas, then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.adminScript: Look at the three pictures. Tell the story. What happened first, next, and last? How did the boy feel? Take a moment to plan. Then say your answer aloud in full sentences.
items.prompt: Look at the three pictures. Tell the story. What happened first, next, and last? How did the boy feel?
items.responseLabel: Planning notes (then say your answer aloud)
frames: At the end, the boy felt ___.
sayFor: tell what happens in all three pictures
tell how the boy feels at the beginning and the end

models.A: Boy sad. Puppy gone. Shelter. Puppy back. Happy.
models.B: First, the boy is sad because his puppy is gone. Next, he and his mom go to the animal shelter. Finally, the worker finds the puppy and the boy hugs it.
models.C: First, the boy felt very sad because his puppy was missing, and he was holding an empty leash. Next, he and his mother went to the animal shelter and asked a worker for help. Finally, the shelter worker found the brown puppy, and the boy gave it a big hug. At the end, he felt so happy and thankful.

items.correct: Strong answer (model): First, the boy felt very sad because his puppy was missing, and he was holding an empty leash. Next, he and his mother went to the animal shelter and asked a worker for help. Finally, the shelter worker found the brown puppy, and the boy gave it a big hug. At the end, he felt so happy and thankful.
items.hint: Say one or two sentences for each picture. Tell how the boy feels.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Say your answer out loud. Listen to the models to hear how answers grow.

picture.alt: Three pictures in order. 1: A sad boy stands outside his house holding an empty leash next to an empty dog house. 2: The boy and his mother talk to a worker at the animal shelter. 3: The shelter worker has found the brown puppy, and the boy hugs it happily.

sections.title: Writing: Weather Stories
sections.directions: Read each task. Look at the picture if there is one. Plan your ideas, then write in complete sentences. Use the word bank and sentence frames. Check your writing when you finish.

items.title: A Rainy Walk
items.prompt: Look at the four pictures. Write a story about the girl's walk to school. Tell what happened first, next, then, and last. Tell how she felt. Write 4 to 6 sentences.
writeFor: one or more sentences for each picture

models.A: Girl walk. Rain. Friend umbrella. School.
models.B: First, a girl walked to school in the sun. Next, it started to rain and she got wet. Then her friend came with an umbrella. Finally, they walked to school together.
models.C: First, Lina walked to school on a sunny morning with her backpack. Next, dark clouds filled the sky, and rain poured down until she was wet and sad. Then her friend Ana ran over and held her red umbrella over both of them. Finally, the two friends arrived at school together, smiling. Lina felt thankful to have such a kind friend.

items.correct: Strong response (model): First, Lina walked to school on a sunny morning with her backpack. Next, dark clouds filled the sky, and rain poured down until she was wet and sad. Then her friend Ana ran over and held her red umbrella over both of them. Finally, the two friends arrived at school together, smiling. Lina felt thankful to have such a kind friend.
items.hint: Write about each picture in order. Give the girl and her friend names.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Read your writing again when you finish and fix one thing.

picture.alt: Four pictures in order. 1: A girl with a backpack walks to school in the sunshine. 2: Dark clouds come, rain pours down, and the girl gets wet and looks sad. 3: Her friend comes over with a red umbrella. 4: The two friends share the umbrella and arrive at school together, smiling.

items.title: The Best Season
items.prompt: Which season is the best: spring, summer, fall, or winter? Write your opinion. Give two reasons with details about the weather or things you can do. End with a closing sentence. Write 4 to 6 sentences.
items.responsePlaceholder: I think ___ is the best season.
frames: I think ___ is the best season.

models.B: I think summer is the best season. One reason is that it is warm. Another reason is that I can play outside. That is why I like summer.
models.C: I think fall is the best season of the year. One reason is that the weather is cool, so I can play soccer outside without getting too hot. Another reason is that the leaves turn orange and red, and my sister and I jump in big piles of them. That is why fall is my favorite season.

items.correct: Strong response (model): I think fall is the best season of the year. One reason is that the weather is cool, so I can play soccer outside without getting too hot. Another reason is that the leaves turn orange and red, and my sister and I jump in big piles of them. That is why fall is my favorite season.
items.hint: Choose one season first. Then give two reasons.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Read your writing again when you finish and fix one thing.
